subject: Agriculture
title: Nematodes: Invisible Destroyers
description: Learn Nematodes: Invisible Destroyers in one minute.

hook.text: Plant-parasitic nematodes cause $150 billion in crop losses annually—yet most farmers never see them.

buildup.text: These microscopic worms live in soil and burrow into roots, blocking nutrient and water uptake.

discovery.text: Root-knot nematodes cause swollen galls on roots. Plants wilt and stunt—looking drought-stressed when soil is moist.

twist.text: Nematode damage is often misdiagnosed as nutrient deficiency or drought. The real culprit hides underground.

climax.text: Chemical nematicides are toxic and being withdrawn. Resistant varieties and biological controls are the future.

punchline.text: The most expensive pest on Earth is too small to see without a microscope.

quiz.question: How much do plant-parasitic nematodes cost agriculture annually?
